name: Microsoft for Education Daily
tldr: Room to learn: Windows gets snappier on 8 GB PCs, an Ontario board opens Copilot's Study and Learn to Grades 9-12, and Imagine Cup keeps a category for students.
window: Window: the 24 hours to 05:00 AEDT, Wed 4 Nov 2026 (Tuesday 3 Nov in the US), plus one This-week item: Imagine Cup 2027 (2 Nov).
notes: This week: Imagine Cup 2027 (Microsoft for Startups, 2 Nov; entrants 18+). Windows' 8 GB gains are Microsoft's 'up to' figures from its telemetry and lab tests; rollout varies by device.

HWDSB set 3 Nov to enable Copilot for Grades 9-12, through Study and Learn only, per its own notice. OneDrive's access requests (due Jan 2027) and Teams' blocked file types (due Dec) are roadmap features in development.
Screenshots are the publishers' public pages as captured on 4 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
ROOM TO LEARN. 🎒

The last 24h for education:

stories.title: Windows 11 is now up to 20% more responsive on PCs with 8 GB of memory
stories.summary: Microsoft says Windows 11 on 8 GB PCs is up to 20% more responsive, multitasking is up to 40% faster in its lab test, and up to 2 GB more of your active data stays in memory, so open apps and tabs are less likely to reload. Get it with Windows 11 version 26H2, build 26300.9818 or later; rollout varies by device.

stories.title: Ontario's HWDSB set 3 November to enable Copilot for Grades 9-12, through Study and Learn only
stories.summary: The Hamilton-Wentworth District School Board says Microsoft Copilot will be enabled for its Grade 9 to 12 students only through Study and Learn, a student-focused experience, with ongoing learning and guidance for staff. Its principle: technology must support student learning and well-being, not drive it.

stories.title: Arnis turns any place on Earth into a Minecraft world, and teachers are using it in class
stories.summary: An open-source project profiled by GitHub turns OpenStreetMap data into Minecraft worlds you can explore, with close to 900,000 downloads. Its maintainer's favourite use is in schools: teachers generate their city or a park, every student improves the same area, and the class looks at the results together.

stories.title: OneDrive is due to let you answer access requests right in the Share dialog
stories.summary: When people ask for access to a file, folder or library, anyone who can share it will see pending requests in the Share dialog and can approve or decline them one by one or in bulk, choose the access level and message the requester first. Handy, for example, when a whole class asks for the same file.

stories.title: Teams admins will be able to choose which risky file types are blocked
stories.summary: Teams is expanding admin controls for Weaponizable File Protection: admins will be able to customise which file types are blocked in Teams to fit their security requirements, or keep Microsoft's recommended default list. It's in development on the Microsoft 365 roadmap for December.

stories.title: Azure Migrate can now discover and assess NetApp and Dell file storage, in preview
stories.summary: Azure Migrate now supports discovery and assessment of on-premises network-attached storage, so IT teams can plan migrations of Dell PowerScale (OneFS) and NetApp ONTAP storage to Azure. Its appliance connects directly to the NAS clusters.

stories.title: .NET Conf 2026 is free and online from 10 to 13 November, with the .NET 11 launch
stories.summary: A free, four-day virtual conference: Microsoft's product teams on 10-11 November, opening with the .NET 11 launch keynote at 8am PST, then community-led talks on 12-13 November. You can also organise a local .NET Conf event until 15 January 2027.

stories.title: Imagine Cup 2027 opens to more early-stage startups, and students keep their own category
stories.summary: Microsoft's Imagine Cup now spans seven categories for early-stage startups, including a dedicated Student Startup category with its own judging and a Top Student Startup prize of $25,000 cash and $250,000 in Startup credits. Entrants must be at least 18; applications are open until 28 February 2027.

stories.title: Microsoft warns of fake downloads that quietly turn PCs into money-makers for someone else
stories.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence found trojanized installers posing as cracked software, free games, Roblox executors and auto-clickers that silently turn PCs into proxies, distributed-computing nodes or adware hosts. Its advice: block untrusted software sources and turn on potentially unwanted app protection.

stories.title: Edge now turns off notifications from sites caught pushing scams
stories.summary: Since Edge 156, when Microsoft Defender SmartScreen or Scareware blocker detects a scam pushed through a website notification, Edge switches off that site's notifications and explains why the next time it starts; you can review or undo it in Settings. A new Block and report option lets you report notification lures.

stories.title: The Elder Scrolls VI finally has a name: Sentinel
stories.summary: Bethesda revealed the subtitle in a new teaser as it celebrated 40 years: the follow-up to Skyrim is The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. There's still no release date.

stories.title: Game Pass adds Football Manager 27 now, Warhammer Survivors on 10 November and Thronefall on 11 November
stories.summary: November's first Game Pass wave: Football Manager 27 is out on PC Game Pass now, Warhammer Survivors arrives on 10 November, and Thronefall, a strategy game where you build a kingdom by day and defend it by night, follows on 11 November. Tiers vary by game; dates are US dates.

transcript.t: It's Wednesday, and this is the Microsoft for Education Daily.
Here are the last 24 hours at Microsoft, in 3 minutes.
Room to learn. On 8GB PCs, Windows 11 is now up to 20% more responsive.
Multitasking's up to 40% faster in Microsoft's lab, and open tabs reload less.
In Ontario, the Hamilton-Wentworth board set November 3 to switch on Copilot for grades 9 to 12.
Students get Study and Learn only. The board's rule?
Technology supports learning; it doesn't drive it.
Meanwhile, teachers are generating their own city in Minecraft with Arnis, an open-source tool.
Every student improves the same park, then the class compares. Nearly 900,000 downloads so far.
Teachers, in January OneDrive's due to let you approve a whole class's access requests at once.
Due in December, Teams admins can choose which risky file types to block, or keep Microsoft's list.
For university IT, Azure Migrate can now discover and assess NetApp and Dell file storage, in preview.
For student coders, .NET Conf is free online from November 10, launching .NET 11.
Got a student startup? Imagine Cup is opening up to more startups, but students keep their own category.
The top student startup wins $25,000 plus credits; applications close February 28.
The fine print? Fake free games, Roblox cheat tools and cracked apps are quietly hijacking PCs for profit.
Meanwhile, Edge now automatically switches off notifications from sites caught pushing scams.
After hours? The Elder Scrolls VI finally has a name: Sentinel.
No release date yet.
Game Pass gets Football Manager 27 on PC now, and Warhammer Survivors on November 10.
Then Thronefall on the 11th: build a kingdom by day, defend it by night.
Snappier 8GB laptops, an AI tutor for teens, a stage for student founders: that's room to learn.
Zoom out, and it never stops shipping.
Today's board: shipped. Tomorrow's: already building.
That's one day of updates. Imagine a whole year.
You've been watching the Microsoft for Education Daily.
Same time tomorrow?
